I understand this a bit better now, but I still have one question: without `CSIDriver.Spec.FSGroupPolicy`, ownership change works for CSI ephemeral inline volumes if *no* FSType is specified. We know because the test in PMEM-CSI relies on it. But if FSType is specified, it either panics (without this PR) or skips ownership changes (with this PR) - right?

I was hoping that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102651 would be resolved as "ownership change works", not as "avoid the panic and leave ownership unchanged".

Is FSGroupPolicy going beta in 1.22?

> I understand this a bit better now, but I still have one question: without CSIDriver.Spec.FSGroupPolicy, ownership change works for CSI ephemeral inline volumes if no FSType is specified. We know because the test in PMEM-CSI relies on it. But if FSType is specified, it either panics (without this PR) or skips ownership changes (with this PR) - right?

The entire mechanism of looking in to access modes and fstype is a hack and we want to move away from it. It is a legacy mechanism. Going forward we expect cluster admins/CSI drivers to configure `FSGroupPolicy` field in `CSIDriver`. The feature is already beta in 1.20  (and should have probably gone GA in 1.22 but it might be too late for that).

> The feature is already beta in 1.20

I had looked at the documentation for 1.21.1 and it still said "alpha field":
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.21.1/staging/src/k8s.io/api/storage/v1/types.go#L355-L356

Looks like this was fixed on master and not backported.

In that case I waive all of my concerns. This looks like the right solution also for 1.20 and 1.21, and 1.19 didn't have the problem.

issue_context.title: kubelet panics on creation of inline ephemeral volume with FSType specified
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
kubelet panics on creation of inline ephemeral volume with FSType specified.

#### What you expected to happen:
creation of inline ephemeral volume succeeds with FSType specified.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
no existing isolated test case. Happens during e2e testing of pmem-csi.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): The pmem-csi CI system where this was detected, runs same tests on k8s systems with 1.19 and 1.20. The problem occurs in testing on 1.20 system, problem does not occur on 1.19 system.

- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: pmem-csi tests run on cluster formed by few qemu-based systems running Fedora-33 and emulated pmem storage.

The issue has been seen in e2e testing in [pmem-csi](https://github.com/intel/pmem-csi), where a new test was
recently introduced that creates a pod with an inline ephemeral volume.

If the related VolumeSource has filesystem type set to empty "", or FSType is omitted in spec,
then the pod creation works OK. In that case, pmem-csi chooses it's default fstype which is `ext4`.

Example of working definition of VolumeSource:
```
   fstype := ""
   vsource := v1.VolumeSource{
           CSI: &v1.CSIVolumeSource{
                   Driver: "pmem-csi.intel.com",
                   FSType: &fstype,
                   VolumeAttributes: map[string]string{
                           "size": "110Mi",
                   },
           },
   }
```

If the filesystem type in the VolumeSource is set to `ext4` or `xfs`
then kubelet fails to create the volume and pod. A panic trace is written in the node kubelet log and the creation will be retried few times,

and volume are created, formatted with mkfs, mounted and NodePublishVolume returns OK.
Same request is received few times with increasing time interval.
